components.css: :host{--color-wall:#2b2e33;--color-panel:#e3e5e4;--color-card:#fbfbfa;--color-chalk:#f4f5f2;--color-ink:#17191c;--color-ink-soft:#4b5058;--color-ink-faint:#6b7079;--color-tape-yellow:#ffd23f;--color-tape-blue:#2f64e6;--color-tape-red:#d6392b;--ease-out-expo:cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);} .ds-route{display:flex;align-items:center;list-style:none;margin:0;padding:20px;background:#fbfbfa;border-radius:14px;max-width:360px;} .ds-hold{width:30px;height:28px;border-radius:46% 54% 40% 60%/55% 45% 55% 45%;background:radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%,#ffe78a,#ffd23f 55%,#c99a00);box-shadow:0 5px 8px rgb(0 0 0/0.3);position:relative;flex:none;} .ds-hold::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset:50% auto auto 50%;width:6px;height:6px;margin:-3px;border-radius:50%;background:#15171a;} .ds-reached::before{content:'';position:absolute;left:8px;top:6px;width:12px;height:7px;border-left:3px solid #eef0ec;border-bottom:3px solid #eef0ec;transform:rotate(-45deg);z-index:1;} .ds-current{width:38px;height:35px;} .ds-ghost{opacity:.3;filter:grayscale(1);} .ds-link{flex:1;height:0;margin:0 4px;border-top:2px solid rgb(23 25 28/0.4);} .ds-ahead{border-top-style:dashed;border-top-color:rgb(23 25 28/0.15);}

narrative.overview:
The mentor sets the route and the mentee climbs it. The system is a bouldering gym: a graphite plywood wall drilled with a T-nut bolt grid, resin holds bolted to it, laminated route cards hung beside it, and strips of grade tape that name every route and every state. A roadmap is a graded, taped route; a milestone is a hold; progress is a chalk tick.

The world has two grounds, chosen by what the surface is for. Persuade surfaces (the landing, the auth aside, the route heroes at the top of dashboard and roadmap screens, the app sidebar) stand on the graphite wall. Operate surfaces (dashboard body, browse, routes, messages, profile, every form) sit on the light panel with laminated route cards on top. This split comes from product truth rather than the metaphor: mentees and mentors use MentorMatch for dense, repeated working sessions (tasks, roadmaps, messages, long forms) and the product targets WCAG 2.1 AA. Long reading and form entry on a light ground keep body ink at high contrast (13.9:1 on the panel), while the wall is reserved for the moments that carry identity.

Accent is scarce and semantic. The grade-tape colours are the only accents and each one means something. Type is one variable family, Archivo, pushed wide and black for display and held at normal width for UI, with Permanent Marker appearing only where a setter would write by hand: on tape.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite wall (bolt-hole dot grid, 52px pitch) for identity moments; light dotted panel for working screens.
Laminated route cards (#fbfbfa, 14px corners, soft card shadow) carry all operate-mode content.
Grade-tape colours as the only accents, each bound to one meaning.
Archivo wide-black display (wdth 112, weight 850) against plain Archivo UI; marker face only on tape.
Holds as the unit of progress: reached holds ticked in chalk, holds ahead drawn as ghosts.
One authored motion moment: the route is set bottom-up on the landing.

rules.name: The Tape Means Something Rule
rules.body: Every accent is a grade-tape colour with one job: yellow = primary action, active nav, brand holds; blue = current (current hold, focus ring); green = reached / done; red = error / destructive. Pink is resin, never state. If a colour is not doing one of those jobs, it is ink, chalk or a neutral.

rules.name: The Ground By Mode Rule
rules.body: Persuade surfaces stand on the graphite wall; Operate surfaces sit on the light panel with laminated route cards. A working screen gets at most one wall band (a route hero) above its panel body.

rules.name: The Ink Link Rule
rules.body: Hyperlinks are ink with a 2px underline at 30% ink, darkening to full ink on hover. Links are never tape blue; blue already means "current".

rules.name: The Inherited Palette Rule
rules.body: The legacy names (gray, blue, green, yellow, red, brand-*) and the shadcn semantic tokens are remapped onto this world in the theme so older screens inherit it. New code uses the world names (wall, panel, card, chalk, ink, tape-*).

rules.name: The Marker Only On Tape Rule
rules.body: Permanent Marker appears inside a tape strip and nowhere else: not headings, not buttons, not body.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone; there is no small label above them. Attribution ("Set by your mentor", setter / mentee names) rides on chalk or yellow tape tags beside the content.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Dates, times, table cells and scores use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Laminate Rule
rules.body: Content never floats free on the panel; it sits on a route card with the card shadow. Lift is for things that cover other things.

dos: **Do** put identity moments (landing, auth aside, route heroes, sidebar) on the graphite wall and working screens on the light panel with route cards.
**Do** keep tape-yellow for the primary action, active nav, selected / shared skills and brand holds; use tape-blue only for "current" and focus.
**Do** draw a route in one resin colour, grade it Start, V1, V2..., tick reached holds in chalk and ghost the holds ahead.
**Do** set every app h1 in the display voice (Archivo 850, wdth 112) and keep body text ink or ink-soft on laminate or panel.
**Do** style hyperlinks as ink with a 2px underline at 30% ink.
**Do** use the world token names (wall, panel, card, chalk, ink, tape-*) in new code.
**Do** give every route and hold a text equivalent, and keep the 3px tape-blue focus ring visible.
donts: **Don't** use a grade-tape colour as decoration without its meaning, and don't give pink a state meaning.
**Don't** set Permanent Marker outside a tape strip.
**Don't** put an eyebrow or kicker label above a heading; attribution goes on a tape tag.
**Don't** mix resin colours within a single route.
**Don't** put ink-faint text on the bare panel; it is for laminate only.
**Don't** add a second authored animation; state changes stay short and on the expo ease-out.
